content: {"summary":"Node 02’s root disk filled because the OpenSearch application log under /var/log/opensearch was not rotated, growing to ~29 GB (≈1 GB per day) after the node rebuild, causing ENOSPC. The cleanup procedure is to restore the missing logrotate configuration with copytruncate, then force a rotation (logrotate ‑f) and, if needed, truncate the still‑open file or restart the process.","likely_cause":"Missing logrotate configuration for OpenSearch logs allowed the log file to grow unchecked and fill the root disk.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"one *.log file under /var/log/opensearch/ at about 29 GB","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#1"],"quote":"one `*.log` file under `/var/log/opensearch/` at about 29 GB."},{"text":"The log grows about 1 GB a day","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#2"],"quote":"The log grows about 1 GB a day."},{"text":"Check its logrotate file under /etc/logrotate.d/, run sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/<name>","evidence_ids":["RB-008#1"],"quote":"Check its logrotate file under `/etc/logrotate.d/`, run `sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/<name>`."},{"text":"put the logrotate file back from config management (with copytruncate, because OpenSearch keeps the file open)","evidence_ids":["INC-0101#1"],"quote":"put the logrotate file back from config management (with `copytruncate`, because OpenSearch keeps the file open)."}],"next_checks":["Verify that the OpenSearch logrotate file exists on all search‑cluster nodes","Confirm copytruncate is set so the log file can be rotated while OpenSearch holds it open","Monitor /var usage alerts and ensure tickets are owned promptly","Check for any remaining open file handles with lsof +L1 after rotation"]}
